nutshell: Sketch-based person ReID must handle subjective drawing-style variation across artists, but collecting a large diverse dataset of pedestrian sketches is impractical. AIP instead leverages cheap, stylistically diverse non-pedestrian sketch-RGB data (the Sketchy dataset) through a two-stage CLIP prompt-tuning framework - category/instance-level alignment first, then an input-aware style prompt generator - to generalize to unseen subjective sketch styles in zero-shot pedestrian sketch ReID.
contributions: First work to target cross-category subjective style generalization for sketch-based person ReID: uses non-pedestrian sketch-RGB pairs (Sketchy, ~70K sketches across 125 categories) as a proxy source of style diversity, rather than requiring more pedestrian sketch data.

Adaptive Incremental Prompt-tuning (AIP), a two-stage CLIP prompt-tuning pipeline: Stage 1 (Category-aware Instance Alignment) learns category-wise and globally-shared visual prompts, using an Adaptive Category-Decoupled Embedding (subtracting the category text anchor from image features) and a meta-learning-style Meta-Optimized Instance Alignment (inner-loop update on non-pedestrian pairs, outer-loop validated against pedestrian pairs) so non-pedestrian fine-grained knowledge doesn't overwhelm pedestrian-specific learning.

Stage 2 (Input-aware Style Alignment): a style prompt generator (conv patch embedding + 3 transformer blocks) that dynamically refines the learned prompts per input sketch, trained with a style-consistency loss that minimizes KL divergence between the RGB-gallery similarity distributions of same-identity sketches drawn in different subjective styles - a purely relational way to enforce style invariance without needing pixel-level style-paired supervision.

New state-of-the-art zero-shot results on PKU-Sketch and MaSk1k, with an ablation (RQ1) explicitly showing that naively adding the same non-pedestrian data (via mixing or sequential fine-tuning, without AIP's structured alignment) gives much smaller gains and can even slightly hurt performance - isolating the gain to the proposed method rather than the extra data alone.
deficiencies: PKU-Sketch is very small (200 identities, 1 sketch + 2 RGB photos each), and Table 2 shows both AIP and the CLIP-base ablation already hit 100.0% Rank-5/Rank-10 - the benchmark may be too easy/saturated at the top end to meaningfully distinguish style-generalization ability from just being 'a competent CLIP-based retriever,' which tempers how much the reported mAP/Rank-1 gaps actually reflect subjective-style robustness specifically.

The PKU comparison against UniReID/AIO is only apples-to-apples for their single-modality 'S→R' variants (which AIP clearly beats); the paper's framing ('comparable or even superior to AIO (S+T→R)') invites comparison against a variant of that baseline that also receives textual descriptions as an additional input modality at test time - a different, easier task setup that isn't a controlled comparison against AIP's sketch-only input.

All quantitative results across Tables 1-4 are single-run point estimates with no variance or multiple-seed reporting, despite PKU's small 200-identity size making mAP/Rank-1 sensitive to just a handful of query outcomes.

The MOIA ablation ('w/o Meta' in Table 4) shows removing the paper's own meta-optimization component actually *improves* Rank-1 (96.0% to 98.0%) even though mAP and mINP drop slightly - a metric-direction conflict on one of the two headline architectural contributions (MOIA) that the text doesn't address or explain.
notable: The style-consistency loss (Eq. 12) enforces invariance by matching each style-variant sketch's *retrieval similarity distribution* over the RGB gallery, rather than forcing the sketches themselves to look alike in feature space - a relational trick that's reusable in any cross-modal retrieval setting where the same underlying entity can look very different (e.g. other imaging modalities, not just hand-drawn styles). Also notable: this paper's own related-work section cites two closely related prior works from an overlapping author list at the same institution (AttnAlign, ref [18], and a 2025 SIGIR paper 'Unified category and style generalization for instance-level sketch retrieval,' ref [11], sharing lead author Zechao Hu) - suggesting an active, tightly-coupled research thread on sketch-style generalization from this Wuhan University group worth tracking if other sketch-ReID papers appear elsewhere in this corpus.
